w10_T4_004912: The community orchard began the season with 28 apple trees along its west path. The volunteers planted 59 new trees in the spring and another 16 in early summer. Later that year disease forced them to take out 54 trees, which were burned at the edge of the field. Every tree still standing gave 4 crates of apples at harvest. A neighbouring smallholder donated 4 crates of his own to the orchard shop, and the committee bought 78 crates from a farm in the next valley to meet its orders. How many crates did the orchard shop have?
w10_T4_004914: The morning ferry queue held 44 passengers when the gate opened. Another 56 walked down from the car park before the boat arrived. The crossing itself takes 25 minutes. During the afternoon 73 more passengers joined the same queue for the later sailing. Before boarding, 39 of the waiting passengers gave up and took the coastal bus instead. In the evening the deckhand counted 3 pieces of luggage carried by every passenger who finally boarded. How many pieces of luggage went aboard?
w10_T4_004922: Sam kept 130 comic books in a crate under his bed, far more than his cousin Ines, who had only a thin pile of her own. He sold 34 of his comics to Ines when she started collecting seriously. Damp in the cellar ruined 3 more of his comics and he threw them out. At a convention Sam made a swap so good that his collection tripled, ending at 3 times what he had carried in. He then donated 193 comics to the hospital reading room. How many comics did Sam have left?
w10_T4_004936: A stone quarry loaded 77 pallets one week, and each pallet carried 8 rough slabs. Half of the quarry's output is sold outside the country. Every slab was later cut into 6 floor tiles at the finishing shed. Inspection found 431 tiles cracked and they were sent back to be crushed. A builders merchant bought 1218 of the tiles, and the council took 857 more for the new town square. How many tiles were still in the finishing shed?
w10_T4_004947: Leo arrived at the model fair with 40 die-cast cars in his case. A clever trade doubled his collection, leaving him with twice as many as he brought. Every car in the case came with 6 loose spare parts in a small bag. Leo and his friend Nadia, who had brought no cars at all, sorted all the spare parts equally into 5 storage trays, and Leo took just one tray home. Each part in his tray needed 8 tiny screws to fit it. How many screws did Leo need?
w10_T4_004948: The mountain hostel counted 132 blankets in its store cupboard at the end of the season. The warden sent 29 of them down to the valley laundry and they did not come back in time. A supplier delivered 61 new blankets the following week. Another 2 blankets were torn beyond repair when a shelf collapsed. A dozen walkers checked in that evening. The warden then gave 147 blankets to a shelter in the town below. How many blankets were left in the store cupboard?
w10_T4_004955: The campaign team loaded 7 vans on the first morning, and each van carried 210 leaflets. A dozen volunteers met them at the town hall. Before noon 174 leaflets were handed out at the market. The printer then ran off 66 extra leaflets and these were added to the vans. Rain soaked 20 leaflets while a door was open, and they were binned. Through the afternoon and early evening 1130 leaflets were posted through letterboxes, and the team notes its walking distances in metres rather than in kilometres. How many leaflets were still in the vans at nightfall?
w10_T4_004958: A small bindery started the month with 58 bundles of blank paper and received 62 more bundles from the mill. Half of its work is for local schools, and the bindery was founded 84 years ago. Every bundle contains 9 large sheets. Each sheet is folded into 4 leaves for the pocket editions. Every leaf is then printed with 7 decorative stamps. Quality control rejected 5100 stamps as smudged, and the foreman counted in 63 good stamps found on an offcut sheet. How many acceptable stamps did the bindery have?
w10_T4_004960: The garden centre opened the morning with 211 rose bushes in its outdoor beds. Before lunch 132 of them were sold to weekend customers. In the early afternoon a nursery lorry delivered 73 more rose bushes. The head gardener then pruned every bush in the beds down to 4 strong stems. A gale in the late afternoon snapped 134 of those stems clean off. In the evening the remaining stems were carried out and shared equally between 2 polytunnels. How many stems ended up in the polytunnel nearest the gate?
w10_T4_004961: The village mill opened the morning with 104 sacks of flour and took in 56 more from the farm cart. Every sack was baked into 5 loaves of bread. Before noon 161 loaves were sold at the mill door. During the afternoon each loaf still in the shop was cut into 5 thick slices for the tasting tables. Every slice was priced at 9 cents for the evening market. When the market closed, the takings were divided equally among the 5 families who own the mill. How many cents did one family receive?
w10_T4_004966: A printing studio pulled 202 proof sheets from its old press. It found 24 of them badly misregistered and destroyed them. Each remaining sheet was then stamped 6 separate times to make a set of impressions. The impressions were filed equally into 6 identical folders, and the studio kept one folder for the archive while selling the rest. Every impression in the archive folder was rated at 5 collector points. Judges deducted 7 points for smudging, and the studio later traded 115 points to another archive. How many collector points did the studio hold at the end?
w10_T4_004977: A haberdashery keeps 123 spools of ribbon in its back room, and it records thread length in centimetres rather than in metres. Over the winter 49 spools were used up on wedding orders. The owner then gave 34 spools to the local drama club for costumes. Every spool still in the back room was wound out onto 9 display cards. Each display card was finished with 4 matching buttons pinned along its edge. How many buttons were pinned in total?
w10_T4_004981: Hana came home from the market with 51 boiled sweets, and the stall sells them by the gram rather than by the kilogram. On the way home 3 of the sweets fell into a puddle and had to be thrown away. She shared what was left equally with her brother Ravi, so the pile split into 2 equal halves and she kept hers. Over the next week Hana ate 14 of her own sweets. She then divided her remaining sweets equally between 2 small tins and posted one tin to her grandmother. How many sweets were in the tin she posted?
w10_T4_004982: A school district ordered 239 packs of pencils for each of its 7 year groups. The stockroom manager, Mr Dane, found 49 forgotten packs on a high shelf and 18 packs in the art cupboard. His colleague Mrs Oyelaran, whose own store proved richer than his, contributed 59 packs from the science block and 54 packs from the library. Every pack in the district holds 7 pencils, and the stock list is kept in single pencils rather than in boxes. How many pencils does the district have?
w10_T4_004998: A city hire scheme owned 226 bicycles at the start of the summer. It sent 102 of them to another city for a season-long trial. The workshop returned 56 repaired bicycles to the fleet, and the council bought 67 new ones. The depot is open 12 hours a day. Every bicycle in the fleet was then fitted with 8 reflectors before the autumn nights. An inspection found 273 reflectors cracked, and they were taken off and binned. How many reflectors remained on the fleet?
w10_T4_005000: A potter finished 53 bowls for the craft fair, and her kiln reaches 1200 degrees at full heat. She sold 39 bowls at the fair itself, and 2 more were chipped while being carried to the van. Half of her income comes from teaching classes. Each bowl she still had was wrapped in 5 sheets of tissue paper. All that tissue was then shared equally among 3 shipping crates, and she travelled with the crate bound for Leeds. Inside that crate the tissue was divided equally among 4 boxes, and she opened only the top box, whose sheets were spread equally over the 5 mugs it held. How many sheets were wrapped around the mug at the front of that box?
w10_T4_005003: The lakeside campsite had 73 tents pitched at the end of August, and it quotes its fees in cents rather than in dollars. Departing families took down 46 of the tents over the bank holiday. A storm wrecked 3 more, which the warden folded away for scrap. The site is 15 kilometres from the nearest town. Every tent still standing sleeps 8 people, and the warden added the 55 sleeping places available in the wooden cabins. Each sleeping place was then booked solid for 3 nights of the festival. How many bed-nights were booked?
w10_T4_005004: A bird sanctuary began the year with 115 nest boxes on its trees. Rot forced the wardens to take down 83 of them. Over the winter the volunteers built 69 replacement boxes, and a local sawmill donated 63 more. A dozen schools visited during the open week. In the spring every box on the reserve held 6 eggs, and the wardens added the 50 eggs recorded in the outdoor pens. Each egg was photographed 7 times for the breeding record. How many photographs were taken?
w10_T4_005010: Ali printed 231 concert tickets for each of the 3 nights of the festival. He found 13 tickets misprinted and shredded them. His partner Meera, who ran the online sales, shifted 399 tickets before the doors even opened, far more than Ali managed at the desk. The box office lists running times in minutes rather than in hours. Every ticket still unsold entitles its buyer to 2 free drinks at the bar. How many free drinks are the unsold tickets worth?
w10_T4_005016: A toy factory had 116 boxes of building bricks in its despatch room and brought in 66 more from the moulding line. The factory weighs its bricks in grams rather than in kilograms. Every box in the despatch room contains 8 bricks. A worker found 49 loose bricks under the conveyor and added them to the count, and 39 bricks came back in a customer return. Inspectors then pulled out 58 bricks with faulty studs and scrapped them. How many bricks were in the despatch room?
w10_T4_005019: Nils had 121 old postcards in a drawer, and postage on them is quoted in cents rather than in dollars. Damp had ruined 22 of them, so he threw those away. A copy shop reproduced every surviving postcard 3 times for an exhibition. Nils and his colleague Petra split all the reproductions equally into 3 bundles, and Nils took one bundle for his own display. Petra, whose drawer held far less, gave him 17 further cards for the same display. Each card in his display needed 2 stamps, twice what an ordinary letter takes. How many stamps did Nils need?
w10_T4_005022: The choir library held 136 songbooks when the new conductor arrived, and rehearsal lengths are written in minutes rather than in hours. A retiring member donated 15 songbooks from her own shelf. The parish sent over 19 more, and a second-hand shop supplied 17. For the tour the conductor had a duplicate made of every songbook in the library, so the collection ended up double its size. How many songbooks did the choir library hold then?
w10_T4_005023: A hill farm had 110 fence posts stacked behind the barn, and a timber yard delivered 58 more before the rain came. The top field runs to 7 hectares. Every post in the stack needed 2 metal brackets to hold the wire. The farmer found 44 spare brackets in an old toolbox and counted them with the others. He then used 131 of the brackets on the gates along the lane. How many brackets did the farmer have left?
w10_T4_005024: A courier began the morning with 57 parcels on his van and collected 17 more from the depot before eight. Every parcel on the van holds 8 separate items for the shops on his round. A dozen shops on the route open late. During the afternoon each item had to be tagged with 5 barcode labels for the new tracking system. In the evening the courier was handed 24 spare labels by the depot clerk and put them with the rest. How many labels did the courier have?
w10_T4_005034: The harbour market took in 236 crates one morning, and every crate held 5 fish. The market has 22 stalls under its long roof. Before nine o'clock 436 fish had been sold to early customers, and a restaurant chain bought 569 more. Each fish that remained was cut into 4 fillets at the back counter. The counter also had 9 fillets left over from the previous day, which were added to the display. By closing time 130 fillets had been sold. How many fillets were on the display at the end?
